drhp.business: The Company manufactures and sells PET stretch blow molding machines used to make bottles and containers for packaged water, beverages, edible oil, personal care, pharmaceuticals, and liquor/agro-chemical packaging. Alongside new machine sales, it earns recurring revenue from spares, components, accessories, installation and maintenance services to its installed customer base. It operates from two manufacturing units in Vasai, Palghar district, Maharashtra, covering the full process from component procurement and machining to assembly, testing and dispatch, and operates in a single reportable business segment.
drhp.end_markets: packaged drinking water and mineral water bottles|carbonated soft drink and hot-fill juice bottles|edible oil containers|liquid detergent and personal care bottles|confectionery jars|pharmaceutical containers|liquor, distillery and agro-chemical bottles|Middle East, Africa and South-East Asia (export)
drhp.expansion: The defining capex project of the year is a new facility at Pelhar, Palghar, built on a plot of close to 2,800 square metres with a built-up area of over 5,000 square metres. It is designed to lift the Company's annual production capability by 40-50% once fully operational, bringing design, assembly, quality control, service and sales teams under one roof for the first time, and includes a dedicated space for live machine demonstrations to customers. Alongside the facility, the Company is readying an all-electric, servo-driven 8-cavity machine capable of producing up to 18,000 bottles an hour, targeted at high-speed beverage and edible-oil packaging customers. Management's stated priority for FY2026-27 is to bring the new facility to full capacity and take the 8-cavity servo machine to market.
drhp.mdna: Global supply chains are being reshaped by tariff actions and manufacturer diversification away from single-country sourcing, opening opportunities for Indian capital-goods suppliers as bottlers and packaging convertors look to de-risk supply chains and shorten lead times.|India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies through FY2025-26, with a supportive backdrop for capital-goods investment by end-user industries such as food, beverages, pharmaceuticals and personal care.|Formalization of the economy and steady credit availability to MSMEs have supported capacity creation among packaging and bottling units that make up a large part of the Company's customer base.|PET stretch blow molding machinery demand is shifting toward automated, high-speed, energy-efficient multi-cavity machines; beverages remain the largest end-use segment and Asia-Pacific leads growth on expanding bottling capacity.|Growth in the machinery industry is driven by glass-to-PET substitution, rising beverage capacity in developing markets, and replacement of older equipment with all-electric servo machines.|Industry themes shaping demand: energy efficiency (all-electric drives, better preform heating, heat recovery), rPET compatibility as brands adopt recycled-content targets, and digitalization (IoT, remote diagnostics, predictive maintenance).|Challenges flagged include low-cost import competition, price-sensitive smaller converters, capex cyclicality, and tightening plastic-waste regulation.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Global supply chains are being reshaped by tariff actions and manufacturer diversification away from single-country sourcing, opening opportunities for Indian capital-goods suppliers as bottlers and packaging convertors look to de-risk supply chains and shorten lead times.
- India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies through FY2025-26, with a supportive backdrop for capital-goods investment by end-user industries such as food, beverages, pharmaceuticals and personal care.
- Formalization of the economy and steady credit availability to MSMEs have supported capacity creation among packaging and bottling units that make up a large part of the Company's customer base.
- PET stretch blow molding machinery demand is shifting toward automated, high-speed, energy-efficient multi-cavity machines; beverages remain the largest end-use segment and Asia-Pacific leads growth on expanding bottling capacity.
- Growth in the machinery industry is driven by glass-to-PET substitution, rising beverage capacity in developing markets, and replacement of older equipment with all-electric servo machines.
- Industry themes shaping demand: energy efficiency (all-electric drives, better preform heating, heat recovery), rPET compatibility as brands adopt recycled-content targets, and digitalization (IoT, remote diagnostics, predictive maintenance).
- Challenges flagged include low-cost import competition, price-sensitive smaller converters, capex cyclicality, and tightening plastic-waste regulation.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The defining capex project of the year is a new facility at Pelhar, Palghar, built on a plot of close to 2,800 square metres with a built-up area of over 5,000 square metres. It is designed to lift the Company's annual production capability by 40-50% once fully operational, bringing design, assembly, quality control, service and sales teams under one roof for the first time, and includes a dedicated space for live machine demonstrations to customers. Alongside the facility, the Company is readying an all-electric, servo-driven 8-cavity machine capable of producing up to 18,000 bottles an hour, targeted at high-speed beverage and edible-oil packaging customers. Management's stated priority for FY2026-27 is to bring the new facility to full capacity and take the 8-cavity servo machine to market.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- distribution: diversified end-use application across multiple distinct segments of the PET packaging economy, reducing dependence on any single consuming industry — evidence: machines are used across packaged water, CSD/juice, edible oil, personal care, pharma, and liquor/agro-chemical bottling
- customer lock-in: recurring, annuity-like revenue stream from the installed base — evidence: Company earns revenue from supply of spares, components and accessories, and from installation and maintenance services to its installed customer base

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Company discloses that it continues to operate in a single reportable business segment — the manufacture, sale and servicing of PET stretch blow molding machines and related capital goods — with no diversification into other product lines.
- The Directors' Report states the Company did not have any Subsidiaries, Joint Ventures, or Associate Companies during the year under review, so the entire business sits within the standalone entity.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Bring the new Pelhar, Palghar facility to full capacity.
- Take the 8-cavity servo machine to market.
- Deepen presence in new export geographies.
- Run the capital goods business conservatively, maintaining a debt-free balance sheet.
